s: A solutions architect must update an application environment within AWS Elastic Beanstalk using a blue/green deployment methodology The solutions architect creates an environment that is identical to the existing application environment and deploys the application to the new environment. What should be done next to complete the update?
o: Redirect to the new environment using Amazon Route 53
Select the Swap Environment URLs option
Replace the Auto Scaling launch configuration
Update the DNS records to point to the green environment

w.y: In Elastic Beanstalk blue/green deployments, once the green environment is running the new version, you use Swap Environment URLs. This swaps the CNAMEs of the two environments, so traffic moves to green with no DNS edits, and you can swap back to roll back.

o.A: Manual Route 53 changes are unnecessary; Beanstalk provides the built-in CNAME swap.
o.B: Correct: Swap Environment URLs exchanges the environments' CNAMEs to cut traffic over to green.
o.C: Replacing the launch configuration updates instances in place, which is not blue/green.
o.D: Editing DNS by hand is error-prone and redundant with Beanstalk's CNAME swap feature.

s: Swap the Environment of an Elastic Beanstalk Application
